entries.speaker: Gian-Carlo Rota
entries.quote: It took me several years to realize what Stan Ulam's real profession was. Many of us at the Laboratory who were associated with him knew how much he disliked being alone, how he would summon us at odd times to be rescued from the loneliness of some hotel room, or from the four walls of his office, after he had exhausted his daily round of long-distance calls.
entries.work: “The Barrier of Meaning,” Letters in Mathematical Physics 10 (1985), pp. 97–99; opening address at the conference “Evolution, Games and Learning,” Los Alamos National Laboratory, 20–25 May 1985; reprinted in Indiscrete Thoughts

entries.speaker: Gian-Carlo Rota
entries.quote: One day I mustered the courage to ask him why he constantly wanted company, and his answer gave him away.
entries.work: “The Barrier of Meaning,” Letters in Mathematical Physics 10 (1985), pp. 97–99; opening address at the conference “Evolution, Games and Learning,” Los Alamos National Laboratory, 20–25 May 1985; reprinted in Indiscrete Thoughts
entries.locus: p. 97, second paragraph, the sentence before Ulam's answer

entries.speaker: Gian-Carlo Rota
entries.quote: For Stan Ulam, this process took place instantaneously, in a flash, unremittingly, day and night, as a condition of his being in the world. He was condemned to seeing the truth of whatever he saw. His word then became the warning of the prophet, the mumbled riddle of the Sybil in her trance. The comforts of illusion were denied to him.
entries.work: Gian-Carlo Rota, “At the Memorial Service for S. M. Ulam,” The Lodge, Los Alamos, 17 May 1984; printed as the foreword to Stanislaw Ulam, Science, Computers, and People: From the Tree of Mathematics (Boston: Birkhäuser, 1986)

entries.speaker: Gian-Carlo Rota
entries.quote: Worried that we might not be ready to bear the burden of those visions, he solicitously improvised daily entertainments, games into which he prodded us all to be players, flimsy amusements and puzzles he built out of his concern that we be spared, as he could not be, the sight of the naked truth.
entries.work: Gian-Carlo Rota, “At the Memorial Service for S. M. Ulam,” The Lodge, Los Alamos, 17 May 1984; printed as the foreword to Stanislaw Ulam, Science, Computers, and People: From the Tree of Mathematics (Boston: Birkhäuser, 1986)
